rules.title: Residential Tenant Protections – just cause required for termination of tenancy
rules.requirement: A landlord may not terminate a tenancy (occupancy over 30 days) without at-fault just cause (12 listed grounds, such as nonpayment, material lease breach, nuisance or criminal activity) or good-faith no-fault just cause (owner or relative move-in, withdrawal from the rental market, a government order, or demolition or substantial remodel). Curable violations require a written notice to cure first, and no-fault notices must meet content requirements and give 30 or 60 days' notice under Civil Code 1946.1.
rules.key_value: Just cause required; at-fault and no-fault causes enumerated
rules.citation: San Diego Municipal Code §§98.0704, 98.0706 (O-21647 N.S.; amended O-21769 N.S.)
rules.quoted_span: A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause.
rules.coverage_text: Residential rental property, meaning any dwelling or unit intended for human habitation, including mobilehome park units. A tenancy is a right to occupy for more than 30 days and excludes fixed-term leases of three months or less. Many property types are exempt under §98.0703.
rules.exemptions: Transient and tourist hotels; short-term residential occupancy; deed- or agreement-restricted affordable housing; subsidized affordable housing (but not Section 8); mobilehomes under the Mobilehome Residency Law; nonprofit hospitals, religious, care and adult residential facilities and nonprofit transitional housing; school dormitories; units sharing a bathroom or kitchen with a resident landlord; owner-occupied single-family residences (renting up to two bedrooms, ADUs or JADUs); owner-occupied two-unit structures; housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years (except mobilehomes); separately alienable units whose landlord is not a REIT, corporation, LLC with a corporate member or mobilehome park management, if the required written exemption notice is given.
rules.penalty: Tenant may sue for injunctive and equitable relief and money damages, including punitive damages, and may raise violations as an affirmative defense. Wrongful eviction damages are not less than three times actual economic damages, and attorney's fees and costs may be awarded at the court's discretion. Noncompliant termination notices are void, and the City may enforce with civil and criminal remedies.
rules.interaction: The Division requires just cause consistent with California Civil Code section 1946.2 and states that its rights are in addition to any existing rights under state or federal law. It does not state that it replaces the state rule.
rules.extraction_note: Added 5-25-2023 by O-21647 N.S., effective 6-24-2023; amended 2-27-2024 by O-21769 N.S., effective 3-28-2024. The new-construction exemption is a rolling 15-year certificate-of-occupancy window rather than a fixed date, so no built cutoff was recorded. Owner move-in requires the intended occupant to move in within 90 days and occupy for 12 continuous months. Leases entered on or after 6-24-2023 must allow owner move-in or the tenant must agree in writing.

rules.title: Relocation assistance and right to re-rent for no-fault just cause terminations
rules.requirement: For no-fault terminations, the landlord must provide relocation assistance equal to two months' actual rent (three months for senior or disabled tenants), either as a direct payment within 15 days of notice or as a rent waiver, regardless of the tenant's income or length of tenancy. If the unit is re-offered for rent within five years after an owner move-in, government-order or demolition/remodel eviction, the landlord must first offer it to the displaced tenant who asked in writing.
rules.key_value: 2 months' rent; 3 months for seniors (62+) or disabled tenants
rules.quoted_span: If the tenant is a senior or disabled, the direct payment to the tenant shall be in an amount equal to three months of actual rent under the tenant’s lease in effect at the date of the notice.
rules.coverage_text: Tenancies in residential rental property subject to Division 7 that are terminated for no-fault just cause.
rules.exemptions: Properties exempt under §98.0703. A tenant found at fault for conditions triggering a government order to vacate is not entitled to relocation assistance.
rules.penalty: A landlord who fails to provide required relocation assistance is liable for not less than three times the required relocation assistance plus actual economic damages. Failure to strictly comply with §98.0706 voids the termination notice.
rules.interaction: Relocation assistance is credited against any other federal, state or local relocation assistance and is in addition to the return of any deposit. The Division supplements Civil Code section 1946.2.
rules.extraction_note: Buyout agreements must exceed this relocation amount or are void (§98.0707(d)). Landlords must also notify the Housing Commission within three business days once the Commission's portal exists.
